questions.q: According to this lesson, what does Kafka itself know about the contents of a message?
options: Kafka converts every message to JSON internally
Kafka automatically detects whether a message is JSON or Avro
Nothing — every message is just a byte array; producer and consumer must independently agree on a format
Kafka enforces a fixed schema on every topic by default
questions.explain: Kafka never parses or validates a message's contents — that agreement lives entirely between producer and consumer.

questions.q: In the lesson's JSON example, what happens when a producer silently renames "amount" to "amt"?
options: The topic automatically renames the field back
Kafka rejects the message immediately at the broker
Kafka accepts the message either way, and the consumer's code breaks silently reading the old field name
JSON messages cannot contain renamed fields
questions.explain: Nothing in Kafka enforces a message shape, so the drift ships and only surfaces downstream, in the consumer.

questions.q: What makes Avro's approach fundamentally different from plain JSON, per this lesson?
options: Avro can only be used with Kafka, never any other system
Avro requires no schema at all, unlike JSON
A schema defining field names and types is defined first, and every message is validated against it before being accepted
Avro messages are always larger than the equivalent JSON
questions.explain: Avro is schema-first — validation happens against a defined schema, not after the fact, and it's also more compact than JSON.

questions.q: What does the Confluent Cloud screenshot in this lesson actually show?
options: The Azure Portal's schema validation page
A diagram illustrating Avro's binary encoding format
A warning banner rejecting a breaking Avro schema change before it can be registered
A JSON parser error in a code editor
questions.explain: It's a genuine Confluent Cloud screenshot showing schema validation catching a breaking change before registration, not an illustration.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say Avro "pairs naturally" with a Schema Registry?
options: Because Avro schemas expire automatically without a registry
Because JSON cannot be used with a Schema Registry under any circumstances
Because a Schema Registry converts Avro messages into JSON automatically
Because a schema-first format needs a central place to store schemas and check messages against them before they're written
questions.explain: Schema-first only matters once something is actually enforcing it centrally — that's exactly what Lesson 15's Schema Registry does.
